hypothesis: The design's own retrain-objective section (Section 4.0) requires a control arm before any claim about the token-aware terms (L_token/L_decorr). The only control arm run so far (docs/design/evidence/w4-control-arm-2026-09-03/) is a 50-step smoke test at this same batch (512): it found the control arm (both weights 0.0) ALREADY clears gate (e)'s PR-rank ratio >= 2.0x threshold on its own, at 2.0191x -- 'NOT DISCRIMINATING at 50 steps' per that README -- and that ~99% of the movement from control to both-on was attributable to L_decorr, ~1% to L_token. This probe re-runs that control arm (token_loss_weight=0, decorr_weight=0) at PRODUCTION SCALE (4000 steps, batch 512, identical otherwise to the failed production run) to see whether the rank-ratio gate discriminates at the step count that actually matters, and whether the held-out/graded/full-pool metrics without the token-aware terms differ materially from the production run's (rank@1 0.8145, graded spearman 0.7463, full-pool recall@10 0.098) -- separating 'the token-aware terms hurt/helped' from 'the merge itself is what did this'.
out_dir_isolation_reason: out-dir is under /akula-data/session-backup-staging/w4-probes/, NOT /akula-data/csd/receipts, because regions/pretrain.py's checkpoint directory is keyed ONLY on a corpus+split-code vintage fingerprint (_vintage_fingerprint), unchanged from the production run. Reusing /akula-data/csd/receipts as out-dir would resolve to the SAME checkpoint directory the production run wrote (memory-checkpoints/d96be64b/), and load_resumable() would find a config_fingerprint mismatch (different batch_size/token_loss_weight/decorr_weight) and raise ValueError, refusing to start -- safe, but it means the probe would never train. A disjoint out-dir avoids the collision so the probe actually runs, while never touching the production checkpoint file.
